subject: Next steps: SDK onramp (auth, routing, tool-calling) + local quickstart
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps: SDK onramp (auth, routing, tool-calling) + local quickstart

Hi Sarah — great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Summary of where we landed:
- Integration surface: you want a server-side Python service for user-facing chat and a TypeScript lambda for background documents ingestion and embeddings.
- Auth preference: your infra team prefers OIDC (Azure AD) for service-to-service tokens rather than long-lived API keys.
- Routing: split traffic by intent (search vs compose) with low-latency routing to a smaller model for compose, higher-quality variant for long-form summarization.
- Tool calling / structured output: you’ll use tool-calling for calendar and patient record fetches; we’ll wire the fact-extraction schema in the SDK.
- Embeddings/rerank: plan to embed incoming docs into your vector DB (Pinecone/Weaviate), use approximate nearest neighbors + lightweight reranker.

Proposed immediate next steps (action items):
1) Tech walkthrough: 30–45min session to go through the SDK quickstart and auth flow (Neha + Marissa + Karthik) — please pick availability for next week.
2) Security packet: I attached a short onboarding checklist and local-samples.zip (contains quickstart repos for Python + TS) — share the SOC2 request with your security team.
3) Local quickstart tasks (priority):
   - Clone the sample repos in local-samples.zip and run the Python chat sandbox.
   - Confirm Azure AD app details for OIDC (client_id, tenant_id) — we’ll provide a template config.
   - Decide on embedding storage (you mentioned Pinecone evaluation).

Mini quickstart (to try right away):
- Python: set REDWOOD_API_METHOD=oidc, REDWOOD_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=..., REDWOOD_OIDC_TENANT=..., pip install redwood-sdk; run examples/chat_local.py
- TypeScript: npm install @redwood/inference; export REDWOOD_AUTH=oidc; npm run dev to test the ingestion lambda stub

Marissa and Karthik — I’ve copied you for technical notes below, please add anything critical for the walkthrough.

Sarah — if you can reply with 1) preferred time slots, 2) whether we should include your security lead on the walkthrough (name/email), and 3) whether you want us to pre-configure an Azure AD test app, we’ll get everything set.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Next steps: SDK onramp (auth, routing, tool-calling) + local quickstart

Nice recap — a few engineering notes to make the walkthrough efficient:

1) SDK language guidance
- Python: use redwood-sdk v0.9+ (examples/chat_local.py). Local quickstart containers the KV cache and a mock routing layer. Command: 
  - python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
  - pip install -r requirements.txt (requirements include redwood-sdk==0.9.2)
  - export REDWOOD_AUTH=oidc
  - export REDWOOD_OIDC_CLIENT_ID=<test-client-id>
  - export REDWOOD_OIDC_TENANT=<tenant-id>
  - python examples/chat_local.py --model rwd-infer-1b --max_tokens 512

- TypeScript: use @redwood/inference@0.9. Sample ingestion lambda is in samples/ts/ingest. Local command: 
  - npm ci
  - export REDWOOD_AUTH=oidc
  - npm run start:dev (runs the lambda stub and an express preview)

2) Auth patterns we’ll demo
- OIDC service flow: short-lived tokens via client credentials + automatic refresh in SDK.
- Fallback API key: for quick PoC only; we don’t recommend long-lived keys for production.

3) Routing config suggestion (simple policy we’ll demo)
- route:compose -> model alias rwd-infer-compose-q4 (lower latency)
- route:search -> rwd-infer-rank-2b (higher quality)
- Use per-tenant routing metadata header X-RDW-Intent for fast policy lookup

4) Structured output/tool-calling
- We’ll provide a JSON schema for the calendar & PRS fetch tools. Sample code in samples/python/tools.shows how to parse the SDK's tool response into typed objects.

5) Embeddings + rerank recommendation
- Use Ada-like 1536-dim open embeddings (we include a mapping in the samples).
- Candidate retrieval: top_k=100 from vector DB, then lightweight neural reranker (model rwd-rerank-sm) returning a score field used to re-sort.

6) Local testing checklist (for your engineers)
- Run the Python sandbox and confirm OIDC token exchange succeeds.
- Run TS ingestion to push a couple of docs and verify embeddings stored in your staging Pinecone index.
- Execute an end-to-end query that triggers reranker and inspect structured output.

I’ll bring the sample commands and a short slide that shows network flows to the walkthrough. Neha — happy to own the code demo.

-Marissa
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
